look_here_first: LOOK FIRST underground: trace a full stolon from shoot to tuber. Softer/spongier stolons and commonly 6–11 mm tubers support yellow nutsedge; compare several mature persistent floral scales (~1.8–2.7 mm), often yellowish brown. Do not ID by yellow head alone.

key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: Perennial sedge with basal linear leaves and flowering culms, often in disturbed moist lawns or sites.

key_traits.label: Underground
key_traits.text: Stoloniferous with softer/spongier stolons, tubers usually 6–11 mm; photograph intact stolon chain.

key_traits.label: Inflorescence
key_traits.text: Umbel-like crown of leaflike bracts, rays and flattened spikelets; often yellow or straw colored but color overlaps.

key_traits.label: Scales
key_traits.text: Persistent mature floral scales generally 1.8–2.7 mm; use 1 mm ruler; native variety not assigned.

key_traits.label: Fruit
key_traits.text: Single achene per fertile scale; scaled mature fruit comparison useful.
